main_text.head: CAP. VI. DE OFFICIO PRINCIPIS CHRISTIANI, ERGA EPISCOPVM PROPRIVM.
main_text.p: Abeat igitur Pontifex ille tuus, indignus prorsus qui in Pastorum choro compareat; suus cuique Principi proprius Episcopus & Pastor prodeat tandem; & quid iuris in ipsos Principes sibi vendicet, palàm proferat ac profiteatur.

“Beata ciuitas, cui ex magno dono Dei contigit, vt haberet Principem pium, & Episcopum sanctum; & qui inter se coniuncti animis & studijs toti essent populo sibi commisso regendo [?] gubernando occupati. Sed vtinam non quotidie audire-mus Principes cum Episcopis rixantes vel de præcedentia, vel de emolumentis temporalibus, quasi non essemus Christiani. ---pag. 37.”
main_text.head: I. ANIMADVERSIO.

p.i: Inconsulto Bellarminum Principes pios rixarum, aduersus Episcopos, infimulare.

main_text.p: Beatam esse illam Rempublicam, quæ summo Dei beneficio Principem pium, & Episcopum sanctum, ceu Mosen & Aaronem, mortalibus simul duces nacta est (quo genere consortij nullum in hac vita sacratius aut auspicatius) iuxta Tecum[?] sentimus. Valeant igitur viri contentionum, qui inter
[?] Reading of the word after "iuxta" is uncertain; the initial letter is decorative.

page.notes: The large initial B is joined to "eatam" as "Beatam". The word after "iuxta" has a decorative first letter and is doubtful, marked [?]. In the quotation, the words after "commisso re-" are doubtful (line break with a printed hyphen); "regendo [?] gubernando" is a best reading. The running head word "Differtatio" is printed with long s and read as "Dissertatio". No engraving, stamps or other marks on the page.
